newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND ON START LIST, BUT UNLIKELY TO RACE GS.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ALPHAND ON START LIST, BUT UNLIKELY TO RACE GS.

text.p: French speed racer Luc Alphand, who had been resigned to playing a waiting game in the chase for the World Cup overall crown, was a surprise entry on the start list for Saturday's giant slalom.
Alphand, who has not raced a technical event in six years, leads all-rounder Andre Kjetil Aamodt of Norway by 106 points in the overall standings with two races to go.
After Thursday's Super-G, the last speed event, Alphand had said "the ball is in Aamodt's court now." Aamodt ranks second in the giant slalom standings behind Swiss champion Michael Von Greuenigen.
On Friday, when word surfaced that his coach was considering entering him in the giant slalom as a psychological ploy against Aamodt, the 31-year-old Frenchman reacted angrily.

"I haven't made a zig-zag for six years and I don't want to be a clown," Alphand said before heading to Denver to watch an ice hockey game Friday night between the Colorado Avalanche and the Pittsburgh Penguins.

Alphand, of course, may not actually race but he has the option despite being outside the top 25 racers that qualified for the World Cup Finals based on points. Skiers with 400 overall points or more are eligible to enter any of the finals.
